terms.title: Type Annotation
terms.definition: Explicitly declaring the type of a variable, parameter, or function return value.
terms.explanation: Uses a colon syntax to specify data types and catch type errors during development.
terms.example: let name: string = 'Alice';

terms.title: Type Inference
terms.definition: The ability of the TypeScript compiler to automatically deduce the type of an expression.
terms.explanation: TypeScript infers types when explicit annotations are omitted based on assignment values.
terms.example: let count = 10; // Automatically inferred as type 'number'

terms.title: Interface
terms.definition: A syntactical contract that defines the structure of an object.
terms.explanation: Used to describe object shapes and can be extended or merged across multiple declarations.
terms.example: interface User { id: number; name: string; }

terms.title: Type Alias
terms.definition: Creates a new name for a type, including primitives, unions, and tuples.
terms.explanation: Declared using the 'type' keyword; unlike interfaces, aliases cannot be declaration merged.
terms.example: type ID = string | number;

terms.title: Generics
terms.definition: A tool for creating reusable components that work over a variety of types rather than a single one.
terms.explanation: Captures the user-provided type using type variables (e.g., <T>).
terms.example: function identity<T>(arg: T): T { return arg; }

terms.title: Union Types
terms.definition: A type formed from two or more other types, representing values that may be any one of those types.
terms.explanation: Combined using the pipe (|) symbol.
terms.example: let status: 'pending' | 'success' | 'error';

terms.title: Intersection Types
terms.definition: Combines multiple types into one, requiring a value to satisfy all combined types.
terms.explanation: Combined using the ampersand (&) symbol.
terms.example: type Admin = User & { permissions: string[] };

terms.title: Literal Types
terms.definition: Types that represent exact string, number, or boolean values rather than general primitives.
terms.explanation: Ensures a variable can only hold specific hardcoded values.
terms.example: type Direction = 'north' | 'south' | 'east' | 'west';

terms.title: Any Type
terms.definition: A dynamic fallback type that opts out of type-checking.
terms.explanation: Allows assigning any value and invoking any property, disabling TypeScript's safety features.
terms.example: let data: any = 42; data.foo(); // Compiles without error

terms.title: Unknown Type
terms.definition: The type-safe counterpart of 'any', representing any value safely.
terms.explanation: Values of type 'unknown' cannot be accessed or called until narrowed to a specific type.
terms.example: let input: unknown = 'hello'; if (typeof input === 'string') input.toUpperCase();

terms.title: Never Type
terms.definition: Represents the type of values that never occur.
terms.explanation: Used for function return types that throw errors, infinite loops, or exhaustive switch checking.
terms.example: function throwError(msg: string): never { throw new Error(msg); }

terms.title: Type Narrowing
terms.definition: The process of refining types to more specific types based on runtime checks.
terms.explanation: Uses typeof, instanceof, 'in' operators, or custom type predicates.
terms.example: if (typeof val === 'number') { val.toFixed(2); }

terms.title: Type Guard
terms.definition: A expression that performs a runtime check that guarantees the type in some scope.
terms.explanation: Functions returning custom predicates in the form of 'arg is Type'.
terms.example: function isFish(pet: Fish | Bird): pet is Fish { return 'swim' in pet; }

terms.title: Tuples
terms.definition: An array type that knows exactly how many elements it contains, and which types it contains at specific positions.
terms.explanation: Order and fixed element length matter during definition.
terms.example: let point: [number, number] = [10, 20];

terms.title: Enums
terms.definition: A feature that allows declaring a set of named constants.
terms.explanation: Supports numeric or string-based value mappings.
terms.example: enum Role { Admin, User, Guest }

terms.title: Optional Properties
terms.definition: Properties in an interface or type alias that are not strictly required.
terms.explanation: Denoted by adding a question mark (?) after the property name.
terms.example: interface User { id: number; bio?: string; }

terms.title: Readonly Properties
terms.definition: Properties that cannot be modified once initialized.
terms.explanation: Marked using the 'readonly' keyword before the property key.
terms.example: interface Point { readonly x: number; readonly y: number; }

terms.title: Type Assertion
terms.definition: A way to tell the compiler 'trust me, I know what I'm doing' to override its inference.
terms.explanation: Syntax uses the 'as' keyword or angle brackets; performs no runtime validation.
terms.example: const el = document.getElementById('app') as HTMLDivElement;

terms.title: Utility Types
terms.definition: Globally available built-in type transformations in TypeScript.
terms.explanation: Includes types like Partial, Required, Readonly, Pick, Omit, and Record.
terms.example: type PartialUser = Partial<User>;

terms.title: Partial Utility Type
terms.definition: Constructs a type with all properties of Type set to optional.
terms.explanation: Returns a type representing all subsets of a given type shape.
terms.example: function update(user: User, fields: Partial<User>) {}

terms.title: Pick and Omit
terms.definition: Utility types for selecting or removing specific properties from an existing type.
terms.explanation: Pick keeps specified keys; Omit removes specified keys.
terms.example: type UserPreview = Pick<User, 'id' | 'name'>;

terms.title: Record Utility Type
terms.definition: Constructs an object type whose property keys are Keys and whose property values are Type.
terms.explanation: Used to map the properties of a type to another type.
terms.example: const pageRoles: Record<string, boolean> = { home: true, admin: false };

terms.title: ReturnType Utility
terms.definition: Constructs a type consisting of the return type of a function type.
terms.explanation: Extracts the output type automatically from a function signature.
terms.example: type FuncReturn = ReturnType<() => number>; // type is 'number'

terms.title: Keyof Operator
terms.definition: Takes an object type and produces a string or numeric literal union of its keys.
terms.explanation: Used to restrict parameters to valid keys of a specified object type.
terms.example: type UserKeys = keyof User; // 'id' | 'name'

terms.title: Typeof Operator
terms.definition: Refers to the type of a variable or property within type contexts.
terms.explanation: Extracts the static TypeScript type directly from a runtime JavaScript value.
terms.example: const config = { port: 8080 }; type Config = typeof config;

terms.title: Conditional Types
terms.definition: Types that select one of two possible types based on a condition expressed as a type relationship.
terms.explanation: Uses syntax similar to ternary expressions: T extends U ? X : Y.
terms.example: type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false;

terms.title: Infer Keyword
terms.definition: Allows declaring a type variable within the conditional clause of a conditional type.
terms.explanation: Used to extract nested types within conditional type checks.
terms.example: type Unpack<T> = T extends Array<infer U> ? U : T;

terms.title: Mapped Types
terms.definition: Generic types that build on old types by iterating over property keys.
terms.explanation: Uses 'in keyof' syntax to transform existing properties into new types.
terms.example: type Flags<T> = { [K in keyof T]: boolean };

terms.title: Template Literal Types
terms.definition: Builds on string literal types, expanding into many strings via unions.
terms.explanation: Uses string interpolation syntax inside type definitions.
terms.example: type Event = `on${'Click' | 'Hover'}`; // 'onClick' | 'onHover'

terms.title: Index Signatures
terms.definition: Defines dictionary-like structures when property key names aren't known ahead of time.
terms.explanation: Specifies key and value type requirements for dynamic keys.
terms.example: interface Cache { [key: string]: number; }

terms.title: Discriminated Unions
terms.definition: A pattern combining union types, literal types, and type guards.
terms.explanation: Every constituent type in the union possesses a common literal property used for type narrowing.
terms.example: type Action = { type: 'ADD'; num: number } | { type: 'RESET' };

terms.title: Non-null Assertion Operator
terms.definition: Tells the compiler that an expression is neither null nor undefined.
terms.explanation: Denoted by appending an exclamation mark (!) after a variable reference.
terms.example: const el = document.getElementById('app')!;

terms.title: Strict Null Checks
terms.definition: A compiler flag forcing null and undefined to be handled explicitly.
terms.explanation: Prevents 'undefined is not a function' runtime errors by requiring safe checks.
terms.example: Enabled in tsconfig via "strictNullChecks": true.

terms.title: tsconfig.json
terms.definition: The root configuration file for a TypeScript project.
terms.explanation: Specifies compiler options and files to compile or exclude.
terms.example: { "compilerOptions": { "strict": true, "target": "ES2022" } }

terms.title: Declaration Files (.d.ts)
terms.definition: Files containing type information about JavaScript code without execution implementation.
terms.explanation: Enables autocomplete and type validation for pure JS libraries.
terms.example: declare module 'my-js-lib' { export function run(): void; }

terms.title: DefinitelyTyped (@types)
terms.definition: A central repository holding high-quality TypeScript type definitions for npm packages.
terms.explanation: Installed via npm packages under the `@types/` namespace.
terms.example: npm install --save-dev @types/react

terms.title: Satisfies Operator
terms.definition: Validates that an expression matches a type without mutating the inferred type of the expression.
terms.explanation: Ensures structural compliance while preserving specific literal inferences.
terms.example: const palette = { red: '#ff0000' } satisfies Record<string, string>;

terms.title: Abstract Classes
terms.definition: Base classes that cannot be instantiated directly and may contain abstract methods.
terms.explanation: Subclasses must implement all abstract methods defined in the abstract parent class.
terms.example: abstract class Animal { abstract makeSound(): void; }

terms.title: Access Modifiers
terms.definition: Keywords that control visibility of class members: public, private, and protected.
terms.explanation: Enforces encapsulation boundaries during static type compilation.
terms.example: class User { private id: number; protected role: string; }

terms.title: Parameter Properties
terms.definition: Shorthand syntax to declare and initialize class members directly in constructor arguments.
terms.explanation: Prefixing constructor parameters with visibility modifiers creates and assigns instance fields.
terms.example: constructor(public name: string, private age: number) {}

terms.title: Decorators
terms.definition: A special kind of declaration that can be attached to class declarations, methods, accessors, properties, or parameters.
terms.explanation: Uses @expression format to modify class definition behaviors at runtime.
terms.example: @sealed class BugReport { title: string; }

terms.title: Declaration Merging
terms.definition: When the compiler joins two separate declarations with the same name into a single definition.
terms.explanation: Commonly occurs when multiple interface declarations share identical names.
terms.example: interface User { name: string; } interface User { age: number; }

terms.title: Ambient Namespaces
terms.definition: Namespaces created using the 'declare' keyword to describe legacy global libraries.
terms.explanation: Helps TypeScript understand third-party scripts loaded via global script tags.
terms.example: declare namespace myLib { function init(): void; }

terms.title: Namespaces
terms.definition: TypeScript-specific way to organize code into named logical blocks.
terms.explanation: Legacy grouping mechanism; modern TS code uses ES Modules instead.
terms.example: namespace Utility { export function log(msg: string) {} }

terms.title: Const Assertions
terms.definition: An assertion using 'as const' that signals to the compiler to infer the narrowest literal type.
terms.explanation: Makes arrays read-only tuples and object properties read-only literal types.
terms.example: const colors = ['red', 'blue'] as const;

terms.title: Function Overloads
terms.definition: Allows defining multiple function signatures for a single function implementation.
terms.explanation: Specifies multiple valid argument and return type combinations.
terms.example:
function makeDate(timestamp: number): Date;
function makeDate(m: number, d: number, y: number): Date;

terms.title: Recursive Types
terms.definition: A type alias or interface that references itself in its own definition.
terms.explanation: Essential for typing tree-like structures, JSON structures, or nested lists.
terms.example: type JSONValue = string | number | boolean | JSONValue[];

terms.title: Variance (Covariance / Contravariance)
terms.definition: How subtyping between complex types relates to subtyping between their components.
terms.explanation: Controls type compatibility rules during generics assignment and method parameter overriding.
terms.example: Function parameters are contravariant, while return values are covariant.

terms.title: Module Resolution
terms.definition: The process the compiler uses to figure out what an import refers to.
terms.explanation: Strategies include 'NodeNext', 'Bundler', and legacy 'Node' resolution.
terms.example: Configured via "moduleResolution": "bundler" in tsconfig.

terms.title: Strict Mode
terms.definition: Enables a broad range of type checking behaviors that increase program correctness guarantees.
terms.explanation: Activates flags like noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, and strictFunctionTypes simultaneously.
terms.example: Configured using "strict": true in tsconfig.json.
